issues.description: Method mismatch: Animal.messageOnFeed() return type differs between the problem specification and the solution. The UML/problem statement (problem_statement.md) declares Animal.messageOnFeed(): String, but the solution's abstract class (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) declares public abstract FeedResponse messageOnFeed(). This discrepancy makes it unclear to students whether they should implement messageOnFeed() to return a String (as described in the exercise/UML) or a FeedResponse object (as present in the solution), and it prevents using the solution as a direct reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type of Animal.messageOnFeed() consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix (preserve the original exercise wording): change the solution so Animal.messageOnFeed() returns String and update all concrete subclasses (Pig, Seal, Goat) to return String (removing or refactoring FeedResponse). Alternatively, if FeedResponse is intended, update the problem statement/UML to specify messageOnFeed(): FeedResponse and document the FeedResponse type.

issues.description: Internal solution inconsistency: concrete implementations of Animal.messageOnFeed() in the solution do not share a single return type. The abstract declaration in solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java declares messageOnFeed() returning FeedResponse. Pig (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Pig.java) and Seal (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java) implement messageOnFeed() returning FeedResponse, but Goat (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Goat.java) implements messageOnFeed() returning String. This mixed return-type usage causes compilation errors and makes the solution unusable as-is.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the return type across the solution. Either (A) change Animal.messageOnFeed() to return String and update Pig and Seal to return String (remove or refactor FeedResponse usage), or (B) change Goat.messageOnFeed() to return FeedResponse and update its implementation to construct and return a FeedResponse. Option (A) is recommended to match the problem statement/UML.

issues.description: Concept: the animal feeding response returned by Animal.messageOnFeed(). Problem statement (UML and task text) defines Animal.messageOnFeed() as returning a String (UML: messageOnFeed():String and examples showing literal strings like "Oink!", "Arf Arf!", "Maah!"). Template/assignment materials similarly expect printable String messages when feeding animals. Solution code, however, declares Animal.messageOnFeed() as returning a FeedResponse object (Animal.java: public abstract FeedResponse messageOnFeed()) and introduces a new FeedResponse class. Implementing classes (Pig, Seal) return FeedResponse instances instead of plain Strings. This introduces a new identifier (FeedResponse) and a different method signature than the problem text, making it unclear to students whether they should implement messageOnFeed() to return String or FeedResponse and whether printed output should use the raw String or FeedResponse.toString().
issues.suggestedFix: Align the API across artifacts. Preferred option (A): change the solution to match the problem statement by making Animal.messageOnFeed() return String (public abstract String messageOnFeed()), and update implementing classes (Pig, Seal, Goat) to return the literal messages ("Oink!", "Arf Arf!", "Maah!"). Remove the FeedResponse class and ensure feedAllAnimals() / singFarmSong() print the returned String directly. Alternative option (B): if FeedResponse is intentional, update the problem statement and template to introduce and document the FeedResponse type and change all examples and UML to indicate messageOnFeed(): FeedResponse, explaining how to extract or print the contained message. Prefer option (A) to match the existing textual UML and examples.
